subject: Final grades: portfolio synthesis & narrative delivery
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final grades: portfolio synthesis & narrative delivery

Team — attaching the consolidated scorecards and my draft narratives (see links below and files attached). We need to close grades and the executive-facing narrative by EOD Tue (29th) so the QBR packet can be published Wednesday morning.

High level asks: 
- Please review the per-objective grades in tab "Grades" (2027_okr_scorecards.xlsx). I called out three contested items in column F.
- I drafted short narrative paragraphs for each portfolio (Serving Runtime, Platform, Console/Observability). Find them in the Doc: leadership-qbr-narrative-2027.
- Evidence folder is linked in the Drive; retrospective notes attached (retrospective_notes.pdf).

Specific: I am proposing we bump Serving Runtime latency objective from 3->4 after adding the new KV-cache benchmarks (see Evidence row 18). If you disagree, flag in a reply with recommended grade and one sentence of rationale.

If I don't hear objections by Tue 17:00 PT I will lock grades and send to comms for the exec deck.

Attachments: 2027_okr_scorecards.xlsx, retrospective_notes.pdf

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Final grades: portfolio synthesis & narrative delivery

Thanks Priya — skimmed the sheet. I support the bump to 4 on Serving Runtime latency. The KV-cache benchmarks materially reduce median and 95p for the profile we care about; the remaining p99 regression is an outlier tied to one customer workload that we mitigated with routing policy.

Two quick asks: 
- Add one sentence in the narrative acknowledging the p99 issue and the mitigation we deployed (auto-fallback to conservative kernels).
- Call out the customer impact window (Mar 3–9) in the evidence row so comms can be precise.

If Laura concurs, go ahead and lock it.

— Vivek

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 11:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Final grades: portfolio synthesis & narrative delivery

I reviewed the Platform reliability paragraph and updated the doc with a short evidence blurb referencing the incident timeline and RCA link.

I also uploaded a short excerpt to the Drive with the exact sentence Vivek suggested about the mitigation. Link: https://drive.google.com/document/d/leadership-qbr-narrative-2027 (section: Platform reliability — note appended).

One data ask for Marissa: the SLA impact numbers in the evidence sheet (tab: Metrics) still show a combined delta that looks larger than what I recall. Marissa — can you confirm the aggregated SLA drop is 0.8% for the quarter and not 1.5%? I flagged the cell in the spreadsheet.

— Laura

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 14:45:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Final grades: portfolio synthesis & narrative delivery

Laura — good catch. I pulled the consolidated metrics and the aggregated SLA delta is 0.82% (rounded to 0.8%). The 1.5% figure came from an early, unfiltered export that included internal test traffic. I cleaned the export and attached a short slack-thread export to the evidence (p99_latency_slack_export.txt) showing the filter steps.

I also recommend we add one short parenthetical in the narrative that says: "(incident window isolated; effect limited to a small set of production workloads — see evidence)" — that keeps the tone factual and prevents overstatement.

Assuming Vivek is ok with the wording, I approve locking the Platform reliability grade at 3 and the Serving Runtime latency at 4.

— Marissa

From: Kevin Simon <kevin.simon@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Final grades: portfolio synthesis & narrative delivery

Appreciate the transparency — quick note from the board review: the narrative is clear. Two tiny edit suggestions for tone (non-substantive): 1) in the Platform reliability paragraph, replace "incident" with "service disruption" in the opening sentence; 2) in the Serving Runtime paragraph, add a line about next-quarter mitigations. Happy with the grades.

— Kevin Simon (Acme Product)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Simon <kevin.simon@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final grades: portfolio synthesis & narrative delivery

Thanks all — locking grades per thread: 
- Serving Runtime latency: 4 (bumped based on KV-cache benchmarks; mitigation noted)
- Platform reliability: 3 (evidence and RCA appendices included)
- Console/Observability: 4 (no material disputes)

Deliverables & next steps: 
- I uploaded the final scorecards (2027_okr_scorecards.xlsx) and the redline narrative (leadership-qbr-narrative-2027) to the QBR folder.
- Comms will draft the slide deck tonight; deadline to review slides is Tue 10:00 PT.
- Marissa to update the Metrics tab with the cleaned export (done).
- Vivek/Eng: please confirm the planned mitigations for Serving Runtime in the mitigation-tracker doc by Fri (Apr 2).

Publishing plan: if there are no more objections, I will send the packet to execs Wed at 08:00 PT.

Closing note: thanks for the quick turn on evidence and for surfacing the SLA filter issue — the end product is stronger because of it.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
